title: Ensemble Monitoring 'Diverse Signals > More Compute' Replicated Cheaply

original_idea.body:
# Ensemble Monitoring 'Diverse Signals > More Compute' Replicated Cheaply

**Problem:** An ensemble-monitoring study argued diverse weak monitoring signals outperform simply spending more compute on one monitor, but the finding needs independent replication with a different, cheaper signal set.

**Direction:** Replicate the ensemble-monitoring claim on the APPS backdoor task by combining several cheap, heterogeneous monitors (a small LLM suspiciousness score, a perplexity signal, a code-structure heuristic, a deception linear probe) versus one bigger LLM monitor at matched total compute. Compare AUC at a fixed 5% FPR. Twist: use only signals computable on a single consumer GPU.

**Why it matters:** If diverse cheap signals beat one expensive monitor, control is far cheaper and more accessible outside labs. This is directly useful monitoring-harness infrastructure and a clean reproducibility check.

**Relevant context:** 'Ensemble Monitoring for AI Control: Diverse Signals Outweigh More Compute' (arXiv 2605.15377). Control Tax (arXiv 2506.05296) provides the APPS balanced backdoor dataset and monitor prompts.
